messages:
Aisha Malik: FYI OrchardSupply flagged low activity on our side. Down ~60% on token usage last 10 days, renewal in 5 weeks. Procurement contact switched to L. Harper last week and they mentioned a 2-week evaluation with another vendor. Can we triage? :small_red_triangle:
Tom Reed: Thanks Aisha. Any pattern by team or route? Is this across embeddings/generation/chat?
Aisha Malik: Mostly embedding calls and scheduled bulk jobs. Generation steady but embedded feature consumers dropped. Seats still there but quiet. No billing disputes.
Chang Kim: I'll pull infra traces. Quick check of rate limits and worker queue depth first.
Nina Ortiz: We should offer a short "embedding ops" office hour for their infra + data team. 20-30m focused session might surface easy wins. I'll prepare a 2-slide checklist.
Tom Reed: I'll ping L. Harper with an invite and propose 30m slot. Offer a fast ROI play: increase batch size + use our vector cache layer for bulk ingestion. Could stall their pilot.
Chang Kim: infra snapshot (last 24h):
```
index: embeddings
ingest-rate: 2.4k/hr -> 0.9k/hr
avg-latency: 180ms
vector-cache-hit: 8% (baseline 55%)
queue-depth: normal
5xx: 0.0%
user-agent: orchard-ingest/1.4.0
```
Chang Kim: vector-cache hit is very low. That matches bulk job changes or a client-side SDK upgrade that bypasses cache keys. I'll grep for user-agent variants.
Aisha Malik: Good call. Nina, can you include the simple SDK snippet to keep cache keys stable in the one-pager?
Nina Ortiz: Yep. I'll add snippet + monitoring tiles to watch vector-cache-hit and token-per-req.
Tom Reed: Commercial angle: offer a free "ingest acceleration" tune-up and 2-week extension on trial capacity if they commit to a technical sync. Helps buy time. Thoughts?
Aisha Malik: Agree. Also ask if the competitor pilot requires feature X (real-time streaming or higher recall) so we know whether it's cost/perf or just model accuracy driving the eval.
Chang Kim: Quick follow-up: I found a newer agent string orchard-ingest/2.0.0 in some recent requests. That version's SDK changed how keys are hashed. I'll draft a backward-compatible header we can support on our side for 72h.
Nina Ortiz: If we can patch on our side, we should still run the enablement call to help them revert SDK change. Two-prong: quick server-side canary + enablement.
RenewalBot: ALERT: renewal_date in 35 days. Risk: elevated (usage drop + procurement contact change + competitor trial). Suggested immediate actions: patch (org-scoped), enablement, commercial extension.
Aisha Malik: Owners: Aisha (CS), Tom (AM), Chang (tech), Nina (enablement). Milestones:
- Today afternoon: Chang to roll org-scoped header support as canary (ts 4300001150)
- 24h: Nina to share 2-slide checklist + SDK snippet (ts 4300001220)
- 48h: Tom to secure 30m with L. Harper and propose extension (ts 4300002000)
Tom Reed: I'll keep agenda tight: 10m data, 10m demo (cache/batching), 10m next steps.
Chang Kim: Canary pushed to canary-org=orchard (will monitor). Posting results here once metrics change. :gear:
Aisha Malik: Thanks all. If we see vector-cache-hit recover to >40% in 72h we downgrade risk. If not, escalate to solutions eng for a deeper performance audit.
Tom Reed: I'll include a line in outreach about feature parity checks the competitor might be doing. Keep it factual.
Nina Ortiz: Adding dashboard link and checklist to the follow-up message after I finish slides.
Chang Kim: Canary report (ts 4300001188): vector-cache-hit -> 42% after header patch, ingest-rate back to 2.1k/hr. Early signs promising.
Aisha Malik: Excellent. Closing loop: keep this thread updated and I'll file a renewal playbook note with the new contact L. Harper. :white_check_mark:
